newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: As the U.S. dollar firmed, both the lira and the peseta recovered versus the mark in late trade on Tuesday, lending support to their respective bond markets.
As a result, bonos ended with modest gains after a volatile session as dealers nervously awaited the EU 1997/1998 economic forecasts due on Wednesday.

"We expect Spain to be rewarded. The forecasts will say our country meets the Maastricht criteria. But if Italy is left out of the core countries, that could have a negative impact also for us," a dealer in Madrid said. The 10-year spread over Bunds fell to 108 bps from 113 at midday.
"The market volatility is very high," a money market dealer in Madrid said.

Analysts said they did not expect the Bank of Spain to reduce its key 5.50 percent money market rate on Wednesday, having already cut the rate three times this year with the last move a week-ago. Of eleven analysts and market dealers polled by Reuters not one was expecting a cut.
The six-month bill yields are expected to fall at an auction on Wednesday from 5.447 percent two-weeks ago. Dealers forecast a marginal yield at around 5.35 percent.
